title: 5 Best Back Shavers for Men in 2026: Manual vs Electric Picks
h1: The 5 Best Back Shavers for Men in 2026
description: Of 5 back shavers, the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is best for a safe solo trim; the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS gives the smoothest shave. All 5 compared.
dek: Of 5 back shavers, the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is best for a safe solo trim; the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS gives the smoothest shave.
intro: The Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is the best back shaver for most men: an electric trimmer on a folding, extendable handle that cuts thick back hair to short stubble with little risk of nicks. If you want bare, smooth skin instead, the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS manual razor gives the closest result once the hair is trimmed short.

Back hair is normal, and removing it is optional. If you do want it gone, the challenge is mechanical: you cannot see the area, your arms do not bend that way, and a regular razor on a short handle leaves streaks and cuts. A good back shaver fixes that with a long handle and a head that stays flat against the skin. Pick a manual blade for the closest shave and an electric trimmer or foil if your skin reacts to razors.
quickAnswer: Choose the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro for thick hair and a safe solo trim, the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS for the smoothest manual shave, the Bearback if you are new to shaving your own back, the Philips Norelco Bodygroom 7000 for sensitive skin and whole-body grooming, and the Mangroomer Lithium Max for electric trimming at a lower cost. Trim long hair before any razor touches it.

blocks.p: The first decision is manual or electric. A manual razor on a long handle shaves to bare skin and costs little up front, but it nicks more easily and needs short hair to work. An electric trimmer handles long, dense hair and rarely nicks, but leaves a short stubble rather than smooth skin.

If your back hair is long and thick, start with an electric model no matter what, then decide whether you want smooth skin or a short, even crop. If your back hair is light and you want the cleanest finish, a manual shaver alone is enough.

sections.h: The 5 Best Back Shavers for Men in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: The order weighs reach and handle design, blade or cutter type, wet or dry use, ongoing blade cost and recurring owner feedback about nicks, irritation and missed patches. Details come from maker descriptions, manuals and retailer listings, and kit contents vary by bundle, so check what is in the box before you order.

Mangroomer built its name on back shavers, and the Ultimate Pro is its top electric model. The long handle both extends and folds, so it reaches from the shoulders to the waist and packs away small, and the head locks at different angles for different parts of the back. Its electric blade cuts through long, dense hair without clogging, which is exactly where manual razors struggle, and owners commonly say it is easy to use without a mirror. Because it trims rather than shaves, the finish is very short stubble rather than bare skin, and razor bumps are much less likely. The rechargeable lithium-ion battery runs a full back session per charge, according to the brand. The downsides are a higher price than manual shavers and replacement blade heads that cost more than razor cartridges. If you want quick, low-risk upkeep and can live with stubble, buy this first.

**Pros:** folding, extendable handle reaches the whole back, cuts long thick hair, low nick risk, lithium-ion battery, adjustable head angle. **Cons:** leaves short stubble rather than bare skin, replacement heads cost more than razor blades.

BAKblade is one of the best-known manual back shaver brands, and the 2.0 ELITE PLUS kit pairs a long, curved handle with a wide razor cartridge built to lie flat across the back. The width means fewer strokes, and the curve helps you reach between the shoulder blades without contorting. It is made for wet or dry use, so you can shave in the shower with gel for the gentlest pass or dry for a quick tidy. A manual razor gives the closest result of anything here, which is the point if you want smooth skin. The usual razor rules apply: trim long hair first or the blade clogs and pulls, use light pressure, and expect a learning curve on the angle. Owners commonly report good results after the first couple of tries. The ELITE PLUS bundle includes extra cartridges, which lowers the cost per shave.

**Pros:** wide blade covers a lot per stroke, long curved handle for solo use, wet or dry, the closest finish on this list, brand-sold replacement cartridges. **Cons:** needs hair trimmed short first, higher nick risk than electric options.

blocks.h3: Easiest Manual for Beginners: Bearback Manual Back Shaver

blocks.p: Bearback is a straightforward manual back shaver with a long handle and a head shaped to glide without catching on skin, which owners often cite as the reason they picked it over sharper-edged rivals. It works dry for a quick pass or wet in the shower for a closer, gentler shave, and the plain handle is long enough for most men to cover the whole back alone. Compared with the widest cartridges, each stroke covers a little less skin, so a full back takes a few more passes. Like any razor, it works best on hair trimmed to stubble, with light pressure. Its real appeal is how forgiving it is: if you have tried a razor on your back and come away nicked, this design is aimed at you. It sits below many manual rivals on price, and replacement blades are sold by the brand.

**Pros:** head designed to glide without snagging, long simple handle, wet or dry, lower price than many rivals, easy to rinse and dry. **Cons:** less coverage per stroke than the widest heads, still needs trimmed hair for best results.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Bearback+Manual+Back+Shaver&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Sensitive Skin: Philips Norelco Bodygroom 7000

blocks.p: The Bodygroom 7000 is a body groomer with a two-sided head: a trimmer on one side for length and a foil shaver on the other that gets close without a bare blade touching the skin. That design is why it is often suggested for men prone to razor bumps. Some kits include a long back extension, so read the bundle carefully if back reach is your reason for buying. The tool is showerproof, so you can use it with gel in the shower or dry before dressing, and it rinses clean. It also handles chest, arms and other areas, which makes it a good one-tool answer for body grooming. The foil leaves a slight stubble, and the back extension is less rigid than a dedicated back shaver handle. Philips sells replacement heads, and owners commonly report long service life.

**Pros:** two-sided trim and foil head, showerproof, gentle with low irritation, covers the whole body, strong brand support and parts. **Cons:** back reach depends on the kit including the extension, foil leaves a slight stubble.

blocks.h3: Best Value Electric: Mangroomer Lithium Max

blocks.p: The Lithium Max is a lower-cost electric back shaver from the same company as the Ultimate Pro, with an extendable handle, an adjustable head and a rechargeable lithium-ion battery. It is aimed at men who want the low-risk, no-razor approach of an electric back shaver without paying flagship prices. It trims long, thick hair to a short stubble, so nicks and razor bumps are unlikely, and it is quick once you find the angles. Next to the Ultimate Pro, owners commonly say it feels less premium and has fewer refinements in the head and handle, but it covers the core job. Like every trimmer-style back shaver, it does not leave smooth skin; pair it with a manual razor if you want a closer finish for a beach trip. sections.h: Manual or Electric Back Shaver: Which Should You Buy?

blocks.p: Buy an electric back shaver if your hair is long or dense, your skin reacts to razors, or you just want a fast, low-risk tidy. Buy a manual back shaver if your hair is light or already short and you want bare, smooth skin.

A manual back shaver is a razor blade on a long handle. It gives the smoothest result, costs the least to buy and never needs charging. The catch is technique: you are pulling a sharp edge over skin you cannot see, so pressure and angle need care, and it works best on hair already trimmed short.

Electric back shavers use a trimmer blade, a foil or both on an extendable handle. They cut close but not to bare skin, and they handle long, thick hair without clogging. They are safer if you nick easily and kinder to sensitive skin. Against that: a higher price, batteries that fade over the years, and replacement heads or foils that cost more than razor cartridges.

A common routine is an electric trimmer for the first pass, then a manual razor to finish when smooth skin matters, such as before a vacation. Day to day, the trimmer alone keeps things tidy with almost no irritation.

blocks.h3: What is the best dry back shaver?

blocks.p: If you want to shave without water, an electric model like the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is the easiest dry option, because a trimmer is designed to run on dry hair. Among manual razors, the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS and the Bearback are both sold for wet or dry use; dry shaving with a razor works best on clean, dry skin with light strokes.

sections.h: What Features Matter in a Men's Back Shaver?

blocks.p: You need to reach from the base of your neck to your lower back and across each shoulder blade. Straight handles of roughly 18 to 24 inches cover most men, while folding or telescoping handles help taller or broader men and store more easily. A curve or rubber grip helps you control pressure with your arm bent behind you.

The head angle decides whether the blade lies flat. Fixed heads at a good angle are simple and predictable. Hinged or lockable heads let you set different angles for the upper and lower back, which helps if your shoulders are tight. Avoid heads that wobble loosely; a blade that rocks off the skin leaves stripes and digs in at the edge.

Wide manual blades cover more skin per stroke, which means fewer passes and less irritation. Spade-shaped manual heads are the classic back shaver form, a wide flat blade on the end of a long handle. On electric models, a trimmer handles length and a foil gives a closer finish, and heads that combine both save switching tools. Look for parts the brand sells as replacements, not a disposable head that leaves the handle useless.

blocks.h3: Wet or dry use and battery

blocks.p: A shaver rated for shower use lets you shave with warm water and gel, which softens hair and skin. For electrics, check runtime per charge, whether the battery is lithium-ion and whether the tool runs while plugged in. A tool you can rinse under the tap is much easier to keep clean than one you have to brush out.

The small patch between your shoulder blades is the hardest spot to reach. Before buying, look at the handle length and head angle with that spot in mind, especially if you have limited shoulder mobility. Owner threads on forums such as Reddit return to this point again and again: reach matters more than the motor.

sections.h: How Do You Shave Your Own Back?

blocks.p: If the hair is longer than about a quarter inch, bring it down to stubble with an electric back shaver or a groomer with a trimmer attachment before any razor touches it. A razor dragged through long hair pulls, clogs and skips, and that is where most nicks happen. Trim before the shower, standing on a hard floor or a towel so cleanup is quick.

Shower with warm water for a few minutes to soften hair and skin. For a manual shaver, apply a clear shave gel or foam to the areas you can reach and spread the rest with the shaver head or a long-handled brush. If your shaver is made for dry use, keep the skin clean and dry and use light strokes.

blocks.h3: Work in sections, with the grain

blocks.p: Start at the top of each shoulder and pull down toward the waist in long, light strokes, then do the middle, then the lower back. Let the weight of the tool do the work; pressing harder is the most common cause of irritation. Rinse the blade often. Go against the grain on a second pass only if your skin tolerates it.

Check your work with two mirrors or a phone camera on a timer, and touch up missed patches. Rinse with cool water, pat dry and apply a fragrance-free moisturizer or balm. Shave at night if you can, so the skin has hours to settle before a shirt and a backpack strap rub on it.

Short back hair clings to grout, rugs and bath mats. On a smooth floor such as [vinyl plank](/best-vinyl-plank-flooring/) or tile, a quick pass with a vacuum or a [wet-dry shop vac](/best-shop-vac/) gets it in a minute. Carpet takes much longer, so trim in the bathroom or over a towel.

sections.h: How Do You Avoid Razor Bumps and Itch on Your Back?

blocks.p: Razor bumps on the back are usually ingrown hairs or irritated follicles. They show up more with coarse or curly hair, dull blades and shaving against the grain. Shave with the grain, use a fresh blade, keep pressure light and keep the skin lubricated. If bumps keep coming back, switch to an electric trimmer that leaves a little stubble.

blocks.h3: Exfoliate, but not right after shaving

blocks.p: Exfoliate a day or two before you shave with a body scrub or a washcloth on a long handle. Products with salicylic or glycolic acid, used a few times a week, help keep follicles clear. Skip exfoliating straight after a shave, when the skin is already sensitive.

Itch during regrowth is normal for a few days as stubble pushes through, especially under tight clothing. A light, fragrance-free moisturizer helps, and loose cotton shirts rub less. Shaving or trimming more often, every few days, actually reduces itch for many men because the stubble never gets long enough to turn stiff.

See a dermatologist for painful, pus-filled bumps that keep returning, signs of infection or a spreading rash. Back acne can look like razor bumps but needs different treatment, and shaving over active acne makes it worse. Mention any new or changing moles before you shave over them, and ask a partner or a doctor to check the areas you cannot see.

sections.h: Should You Trim or Shave Your Back?

blocks.p: Trim if you want low maintenance; shave if you want the smoothest look for a specific occasion.

Trimming to a short, even length removes the bulk that shows through shirts and above the collar, causes almost no razor bumps, and regrowth is barely noticeable. An electric back shaver or body groomer with a 1 to 3 mm comb gets you there in a few minutes every week or two.

Shaving to bare skin looks cleanest at the beach or the pool, but stubble returns within two or three days and needs upkeep to stay smooth. For an event, shave a day or two before, not that morning, so any redness has time to fade.

blocks.h3: Does shaving make back hair grow back thicker?

blocks.p: No. Shaving cuts the hair at the surface and does not touch the follicle. Stubble feels coarser because the blade cuts off the tapered tip and leaves a blunt end, and it can look darker as it emerges because it has not been lightened by the sun. The number of hairs, their thickness and how fast they grow stay the same.

A hard line where back hair stops at the shoulders or lower back looks odd. Use a trimmer to taper the hair at the edges of the shaved area so the change is gradual. If you also keep your head short, matching the clipper guard on your head to your body trim keeps everything consistent; our [buzz cut guide](/buzz-cut-guide/) explains guard numbers in millimeters.

sections.h: Back Shaver vs Waxing, Creams and Laser: Which Is Best?

blocks.p: For most men a back shaver is the cheapest and most flexible option: you choose when, how short and how often, with no appointments and no pain.

Salon waxing pulls hair from the root and keeps the back smooth for roughly three to six weeks. It hurts, especially the first time, and needs hair long enough to grip, so you cannot stay smooth between visits. Salons commonly charge somewhere around $40 to $80 for a back wax, depending on the city.

Creams dissolve hair at the surface and last a few days longer than shaving. They are messy to apply to your own back and can burn sensitive skin. Patch-test a small area 24 hours ahead, follow the label timing exactly, and never use them on broken or freshly shaved skin.

Laser hair removal and IPL reduce hair long term over several sessions and work best on dark hair over lighter skin. Clinics commonly quote a full back course from several hundred to a few thousand dollars. Choose a licensed clinic, discuss your skin type and expect maintenance sessions. Home IPL devices exist but are slow to use on your own back.
If you hate upkeep and can afford it, laser is the long-term answer, and you can still keep a back shaver for touch-ups between sessions as the clinic directs.

sections.h: What Does a Back Shaver Cost to Keep Running?

blocks.p: The handle is only part of the cost. What you spend over a year depends on the replacement parts.

Manual back shavers use replacement cartridges or blades that typically last several shaves each, depending on hair density and how well you rinse and dry them. Shaving weekly, blades add up to a modest yearly cost, and bundles with extra cartridges lower the cost per shave if the per-blade price beats buying them separately.

Electric shavers have fewer but larger ongoing costs. Replacement foils and cutter heads last months to a year or more depending on use. Batteries lose capacity after a few years; check whether the brand sells replacement batteries or whether a weak battery means a new tool.

Confirm the replacements are easy to buy before you buy the handle. Brands with proprietary blades can discontinue them and strand a perfectly good handle. Shavers that take widely sold blade formats, or brands that have kept the same cartridge for years, are a safer bet.

Bundled extra blades are worth it when they lower the real cost per shave. Bundles padded with cheap gel, travel pouches or other filler usually are not. Divide the bundle price by the number of shaves you will realistically get from the blades to see what you are paying.

sections.h: How Do You Clean and Store a Back Shaver?

blocks.p: Rinse the blade under warm running water every few strokes and thoroughly when you finish. Shake it out and let it air-dry head up, outside the shower if you can. Water left on the blade dulls the edge and can rust it. Wiping the blade with a towel can damage the edge, so dab or air-dry instead.

Clean electric models the way the manual describes. Rinse waterproof models under the tap, then let them dry with the foil or head removed. Brush hair out of models that are not waterproof with the included brush. A drop of clipper oil on trimmer blades every few uses keeps them cutting smoothly and running cooler.

Do not share a back shaver. Blades can carry bacteria and blood-borne germs even when the skin looks fine. Disinfect blades now and then with rubbing alcohol, especially after a nick, and replace blades that pull or feel rough instead of forcing one more shave.

Store the shaver dry with the blade guard on. Charge lithium-ion models every so often if you only use them every few weeks, and do not leave them in a hot car or a steamy bathroom for long, which shortens battery life.

blocks.h3: A good gift for a hairy chest and back?

blocks.p: If you are buying for someone else and do not know his skin or preference, a showerproof body groomer such as the Philips Norelco Bodygroom 7000 is the safest gift: it trims and shaves chest, back and more, and rarely irritates. For someone who already knows he wants a dedicated back tool, the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is the easiest solo option.

mistakes: Running a razor through long hair

A razor on long back hair clogs, tugs and skips, and that is when it nicks. Trim to stubble with an electric back shaver or a groomer first, then shave. Two extra minutes of trimming saves a lot of irritation and rinsing.
Pressing hard because you cannot see

With no visual feedback, most men push the blade too hard, which causes razor burn and cuts. Use light, steady strokes and let the tool's weight do the work. Check the result with two mirrors or a phone camera instead of making extra hard passes.
Going against the grain on the first pass

Shaving against the grain lifts hairs and cuts them below the skin line, a common cause of ingrown hairs on the back. Shave with the grain first, and only try a second pass across or against the grain if your skin stays calm after several shaves.
Keeping a dull blade too long

A worn blade drags and pulls instead of cutting cleanly, which irritates the skin and leaves patches. Replace cartridges at the first sign of tugging. Rinse and air-dry the blade after each use to keep the edge longer, and never wipe it with a towel.
Shaving the morning of a beach day

A fresh shave can leave redness or small bumps that take a day to fade, and salt water and sunscreen sting. Shave the evening before or two days ahead, moisturize, and give the skin time to settle before sun and swimming.
bottomLine: For most men, the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is the best back shaver: an electric trimmer you can use alone, safely, on thick hair, with the Mangroomer Lithium Max doing the same job for less. If you want smooth skin, the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS gives the closest result and the Bearback is the more forgiving manual for beginners. If your skin reacts to razors or you groom more than your back, the Philips Norelco Bodygroom 7000 covers it all. Whatever you buy, trim first, shave light and with the grain, and moisturize afterward.

faqs.q: What is the best back shaver for men?
faqs.a: The Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is the best back shaver for most men: an electric trimmer on a folding, extendable handle that handles thick hair with little nick risk. For bare, smooth skin, the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS manual razor gives the closest result, and the Bearback is the most forgiving manual for beginners.

faqs.q: Which back shaver should a first-timer buy?
faqs.a: If your back hair is thick or your skin is sensitive, start with an electric model like the Mangroomer Ultimate Pro, which trims without a razor touching your skin. If your hair is light and you want smooth skin, a manual shaver such as the Bearback or the BAKblade 2.0 ELITE PLUS works well once you learn the angle.

faqs.q: What is the best electric back razor?
faqs.a: The Mangroomer Ultimate Pro is the best electric back shaver for most men, with a folding, extendable handle, an adjustable head and a lithium-ion battery. The Mangroomer Lithium Max does the same core job for less. If you also groom your chest and arms, the Philips Norelco Bodygroom 7000 trims and foil-shaves with low irritation.

faqs.q: Can I really shave my whole back without help?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right tool. A handle of about 18 inches or more and a head that sits flat at the right angle let most men reach every area, including between the shoulder blades. Check for missed patches with two mirrors or a phone camera. Men with limited shoulder mobility should choose a handle with an adjustable head.

faqs.q: Will back hair grow back thicker after shaving?
faqs.a: No. Shaving cuts hair at the surface and does not affect the follicle. Regrowth feels coarser because the cut end is blunt instead of tapered, and it can look darker before the sun lightens it. The number of hairs, their thickness and their growth rate stay the same as before you shaved.

faqs.q: How often should I shave or trim my back?
faqs.a: For a smooth look, shave every two to four days, since stubble comes back quickly. For a short trimmed look with an electric shaver, every one to two weeks is usually enough. Many men trim regularly and only shave fully before beach trips or events, which keeps irritation and blade costs down.

faqs.q: Is a body groomer as good as a dedicated back shaver?
faqs.a: A body groomer like the Philips Norelco Bodygroom 7000 works on the back only if the kit includes a long back attachment, and that attachment is usually less rigid than a dedicated handle. It is a good choice if you also groom your chest, arms and legs. If the back is your only target, a dedicated back shaver reaches more easily.
